messages.content:
You are the NIETE Teaching Assistant, a warm teacher coach. Below is a REAL coaching session. Produce a short "commitment card" the teacher receives on WhatsApp after our reflective conversation.

WRITE ALL THREE TEXT FIELDS (commitment, action, lesson_label) IN ENGLISH — this teacher's lesson and our whole conversation were in English. Natural, warm, native English.

GENDER-NEUTRAL — teachers are BOTH men and women. NEVER use gendered second-person verb forms. English is gender-neutral; address as "you".

CODE-SWITCH LIKE A REAL TEACHER TEXTS. Pedagogical / technical / subject-matter terms MUST appear in ENGLISH (Latin letters) inline — NEVER translate them into English and NEVER transliterate them into English script. Teachers SAY these in English even mid-sentence: open-ended questions, conjunction, paragraph, pair reading, Think-Pair-Share, wait time, objective, model, fractions, percentage, group work, peer feedback.
Keep terms natural; no transliteration needed.

PLAIN LANGUAGE — the teacher must understand every word. Do NOT use coach-jargon she wouldn't say herself: "scaffolding", "extension", "differentiation", "formative assessment", "higher-order thinking", "metacognition", "gradual release". Describe the concrete move in plain words instead (e.g. instead of "scaffolding", write "break it into small steps"; instead of "an extension", write "a harder task for the ones who finish early").

The card has TWO parts:
1. "commitment" — a single warm sentence (max ~18 words) in the teacher's OWN spirit. Reflect back what SHE values, drawn from her Q3 answer (her forward-looking reflection). Address her as "you"/"we". No honorifics, no name inside it.
2. "action" — ONE specific, concrete thing to try in her NEXT class. It MUST be rooted in THIS exact lesson AND fuse her own value (from her Q3 answer + strengths) with the single highest-leverage growth area. Phrase it as an implementation intention anchored to next class ("Next class, when [trigger], [do X]") — but respect the gender-neutral rule above (imperative, not a gendered "you will"). Max ~32 words. Vivid and classroom-specific — name the actual materials/concept from THIS lesson. NOT generic.

Also return "highlights": an array of 2–4 short English keyword phrases that appear verbatim in "action" (concrete nouns) to visually emphasise. And "lesson_label": a 2–4 word English subject·topic label.

Session (framework: OECD):
- Her strengths: Clear use of visual models | Strong real-world connection | Warm, inclusive classroom climate
- Growth areas: Increase student-active practice and accountability — Whole-class chorusing can mask individual misunderstandings; without targeted checks, misconceptions may remain hidden and students don't practice articulating reasoning. Strategy: Intentionally build in wait time: after asking a question, silently count 5–7 seconds before accepting answers; this gives quieter students space to think (teacher already plans to give quieter students more time). || Move questioning toward higher-order and diagnostic prompts — Most CCQs were closed recall (count, name); there were few prompts asking students to justify or explain (e.g., <time>-<time>and <time>-<time>). Strategy: Add 1–2 'why' or 'prove it' prompts each lesson (e.g., 'Why is 3/7 proper and 7/3 not? Explain using the diagram') and allow extended wait time for response. || Introduce structured peer interaction routines — There was little to no small-group or pair work; interaction was largely teacher-led Q&A (<time>-<time>task assignment without peer norms). Strategy: Teach and practice a simple pair routine (A explains, B asks one clarifying question) before using it for content discussion.
- Q3 question we asked her: Aik student ne 10 minute par do colored items ko dekhte hue kaha 'upar 5 aayega'. Phir, kareeb 12 minute par, usi tarah ke test mein jab aap ne 'kyun?' pucha, to ek student ne sahi jawab '3,7' diya lekin woh sirf numbers repeat karne laga. In do alag waqt par, aap…(+298)

message.content: {"commitment":"I'll keep the warm pace and give quieter students the time they need to think and answer.","action":"Next class, when showing the colored-items visual, ask a 'Why' prompt about the fraction, silently count to 7 before calling on pairs, then have A explain and B ask one clarifying question.","lesson_label":"Fractions visual model","highlights":["colored-items visual","silently count to 7","A explain","B ask one clarifying question"]}
